baseline.name: Branch-based consecutive-ones counter
baseline.approach: If the current value is one increment the run, otherwise reset it; update the maximum.

archived.name: Arithmetic reset of the consecutive-ones counter

why: Multiplication resets or extends the run for binary values, but computes the same linear scan as a straightforward conditional.
quantitative_comparison: Both perform n run updates and at most n maximum checks. The archive replaces a reset branch with arithmetic; actual machine branches, instruction cost and prediction behavior are compiler/input dependent. No 'how many times faster' claim is established.
tradeoffs: Arithmetic requires the binary-value contract. The conditional version is more explicit; source-level branchless arithmetic alone is not a measured improvement.
evidence_basis: Static source inspection and stated algorithm work/storage model. Comparator is an analytical alternative, not an implemented or timed benchmark. Historical platform acceptance is separate from current local validation.
